title: On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem
core_idea: Defines the Turing machine — the minimal formal model of computation — and proves some problems are undecidable.
why_it_matters: Establishes the ceiling of what any intelligence, biological or artificial, can compute; every result below inherits this frame.

title: A Logical Calculus of the Ideas Immanent in Nervous Activity
core_idea: Neurons as threshold logic units; networks of them compute any logical proposition.
why_it_matters: First proof that neural substrate ⇒ computation; the founding bridge between brain and mathematics.

title: A Mathematical Theory of Communication
core_idea: Information = reduction of uncertainty (entropy); source coding and channel coding theorems; the bit.
why_it_matters: The vocabulary of every loss function (cross-entropy = Shannon information) and of compression-as-understanding. The single most-used equation in LLM training.

title: A Formal Theory of Inductive Inference
core_idea: Predict the future by Bayesian mixture over all computable hypotheses, weighted by 2^(−description length) (algorithmic probability).
why_it_matters: The mathematically ideal — though uncomputable — learner; modern sequence models are its practical approximation.

title: Three Approaches to the Quantitative Definition of Information
core_idea: Kolmogorov complexity: the length of the shortest program that outputs an object.
why_it_matters: "Understanding = compression" made precise; ties Occam's razor to computability.

title: Modeling by Shortest Data Description
core_idea: Minimum Description Length (MDL): prefer the model that compresses the data plus model code best.
why_it_matters: Practical model-selection principle uniting compression and generalization; ancestor of bits-per-byte evals.

title: On the Uniform Convergence of Relative Frequencies to Probabilities (VC theory)
core_idea: Generalization is controlled by the capacity (VC dimension) of the hypothesis class, not just sample count.
why_it_matters: Classical generalization theory — and the benchmark modern deep learning spectacularly violated (see Zhang 2017), forcing new theory.

title: Simplified Neuron Model as a Principal Component Analyzer
core_idea: A single neuron with Hebbian plasticity plus normalization converges to the first principal component of its input.
why_it_matters: Local, biologically plausible rules can compute global statistics — dimensionality reduction for free.

title: Neural Networks and Physical Systems with Emergent Collective Computational Abilities
core_idea: Recurrent binary networks as energy minima = content-addressable memory; physics (spin glasses) applied to neural systems.
why_it_matters: Founded the statistical-mechanics view of neural networks; modern "attention as associative memory" results trace here (Nobel Prize 2024, shared with Hinton).

title: A Theory of the Learnable
core_idea: PAC learning: learnable = efficiently learnable to arbitrary accuracy with high probability.
why_it_matters: Put learning itself on computational footing — learning has complexity classes like computation does.

title: A Learning Algorithm for Boltzmann Machines
authors: David Ackley, Geoffrey Hinton, Terrence Sejnowski
core_idea: Stochastic energy-based networks trained by contrasting data and model statistics.
why_it_matters: First usable learning rule for hidden-unit networks; ancestor of contrastive divergence, wake-sleep, and modern self-supervised losses.

title: Learning Representations by Back-Propagating Errors
authors: David Rumelhart, Geoffrey Hinton, Ronald Williams
core_idea: Compute gradients of error through layers via the chain rule, making internal representations trainable.
why_it_matters: The learning algorithm of the entire deep learning era; still how every LLM trains.

title: The Space of Interactions in Neural Network Models (statistical mechanics of learning)
core_idea: Compute the volume of parameter space consistent with a training set — capacity thresholds and phase transitions in learning.
why_it_matters: Learning has thermodynamic phase transitions; this lens predicts grokking-like phenomena decades early.

title: Multilayer Feedforward Networks Are Universal Approximators
authors: Kurt Hornik, Maxwell Stinchcombe, Halbert White
core_idea: One hidden layer with enough units approximates any continuous function (independently: Cybenko 1989).
why_it_matters: Guarantees representational sufficiency — but says nothing about depth efficiency or learnability (see Poole 2017).

title: An Information-Maximization Approach to Blind Separation and Blind Deconvolution
core_idea: Maximize output entropy (InfoMax) and the network discovers independent sources — without labels.
why_it_matters: Information-theoretic self-supervision works; direct ancestor of contrastive and predictive self-supervised learning.

title: The Lack of A Priori Distinctions Between Learning Algorithms (No Free Lunch)
core_idea: Averaged over all possible problems, no learner beats random guessing.
why_it_matters: Generalization must come from inductive bias matched to the world's structure — explains why architecture and priors matter.

title: Collective Dynamics of 'Small-World' Networks
core_idea: Networks interpolating regular/random achieve high clustering with short path lengths (small-world).
why_it_matters: The architecture of brains, and increasingly of ML systems (MoE routing, agent swarms); a recurring mathematical pattern.

title: Emergence of Scaling in Random Networks
core_idea: Growth + preferential attachment produces power-law degree distributions (scale-free networks).
why_it_matters: Power laws appear in language (Zipf), brains, and model scaling — one generating mechanism, many systems.

title: Self-Organized Criticality: An Explanation of 1/f Noise
authors: Per Bak, Chao Tang, Kurt Wiesenfeld
core_idea: Driven dissipative systems self-tune to a critical point between order and chaos, producing scale-invariant avalanches.
why_it_matters: Candidate explanation for brain criticality (domain 04) and for why edge-of-chaos dynamics keep recurring in learning systems.

title: The Information Bottleneck Method
authors: Naftali Tishby, Fernando Pereira, William Bialek
core_idea: Optimal representations maximally compress X about irrelevant detail while preserving information about relevance variable Y; formally rate-distortion with a relevance constraint.
why_it_matters: The leading formal account of what a "good representation" is; frames deep learning as progressive information compression.

title: An Exact Mapping Between the Variational Renormalization Group and Deep Learning
core_idea: Stacked restricted Boltzmann machines perform the variational renormalization group exactly.
why_it_matters: Physics' tool for scale-dependent structure (RG) ≈ deep learning's stacked abstraction; concrete support for "deep = multi-scale".

title: Deep Learning and the Information Bottleneck Principle
core_idea: Deep networks should first fit (memorize) then compress representations — phases observed via mutual-information probes.
why_it_matters: Predicted a two-phase training dynamic later echoing in grokking (F10).

title: Group Equivariant Convolutional Networks
core_idea: Build symmetry (translation, rotation equivariance) into architecture rather than learning it from data.
why_it_matters: Symmetry is the strongest inductive bias physics knows; equivariant nets show architectural priors can replace data volume.

title: Exponential Expressivity in Deep Neural Networks through Transient Chaos
authors: Ben Poole, Surya Ganguli, Maithra Raghu (with "On the Expressivity of Deep Neural Networks", Raghu et al. 2017)
core_idea: Depth yields exponential gains in expressivity for representing compositional functions, beyond what width can buy.
why_it_matters: Why we stack layers instead of widening flat ones; why hierarchies (brains included) are deep.

title: Understanding Deep Learning Requires Rethinking Generalization
authors: Chiyuan Zhang, Samy Bengio, Moritz Hardt, Benjamin Recht, Oriol Vinyals
core_idea: Deep nets can fit random labels perfectly, so generalization cannot follow from classical capacity control alone.
why_it_matters: Broke VC-style theory of deep learning; opened implicit-regularization and double-descent research lines.

title: Opening the Black Box of Deep Neural Networks via Information
core_idea: Empirically observes the fit-then-compress information phases during SGD training.
why_it_matters: Made information-plane analysis famous — and triggered the field's sharpest theory debate.

title: On the Information Bottleneck Theory of Deep Learning
core_idea: Compression phases largely vanish with ReLU/unbounded activations and realistic datasets; IB theory is not the mechanism.
why_it_matters: The decisive rebuttal — science working; the field now treats IB as a design principle, not a law.

title: Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence and Generalization in Neural Networks
authors: Arthur Jacot, Franck Gabriel, Clément Hongler
core_idea: In the infinite-width limit, training a network equals kernel regression with a fixed kernel (NTK).
why_it_matters: Makes one training regime exactly solvable — and marks its boundary: NTK-lazy networks do NOT learn features.

title: On Lazy Training in Differentiable Programming
authors: Lénaïc Chizat, Edouard Oyallon, Francis Bach
core_idea: Two regimes: lazy (kernel-like, features fixed) vs rich (feature learning); initialization scale selects the regime.
why_it_matters: Feature learning — the rich regime — is what makes deep learning work; connects to grokking transitions.

title: Reconciling Modern Machine-Learning Practice and the Classical Bias–Variance Trade-Off
authors: Mikhail Belkin, Daniel Hsu, Siyuan Ma, Soumik Mandal
core_idea: Double descent: test error descends, peaks at the interpolation threshold, then descends again as overparameterization grows.
why_it_matters: The modern generalization curve; explains why billion-parameter models on "small" data behave well.

title: Deep Double Descent: Where Bigger Models and More Data Hurt
core_idea: Double descent is ubiquitous across model size, data size, and training time in modern deep learning.
why_it_matters: Practical warning: more parameters/data can hurt before they help; scale results have regime boundaries.

title: Visualizing the Loss Landscape of Neural Nets
authors: Hao Li, Zheng Xu, Gavin Taylor, Christoph Studer, Tom Goldstein
core_idea: Filter-normalized visualization shows residual nets have trainable convex-ish valleys; without skip connections landscapes are chaotic.
why_it_matters: Explains why residual connections (ResNet, transformer) made depth trainable — geometry, not just gradients.

title: Neural Collapse: An Analysis of the Modes of Neural Network Classifiers
authors: Vardan Papyan, X. Y. Han, David Donoho
core_idea: At training's end, last-layer features collapse to class means arranged as a simplex ETF — a sharp geometric universal.
why_it_matters: 2025 work unifies grokking and information bottleneck via neural collapse; a concrete geometry of "converged" learning.

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
core_idea: Loss follows smooth power laws in parameters, data, and compute, across 6+ orders of magnitude.
why_it_matters: Made scaling a predictive engineering discipline: you can read next year's loss off this year's curves.

title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (Chinchilla)
core_idea: For fixed compute, parameters and tokens should scale equally (~20 tokens/parameter) — most 2021-era models were badly undertrained.
why_it_matters: The recipe behind every efficient model since (LLaMA etc.); GPT-3-sized results from 4× smaller models.

title: Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets
core_idea: Networks memorize quickly but suddenly generalize long after overfitting, when trained past the point of zero training loss.
why_it_matters: Separates memorization from understanding in time; a lab model of "aha moment" learning.

title: Towards Understanding Grokking: An Effective Theory of Representation Learning
authors: Ziming Liu, Ouail Kitouni, Mike Nolte, Eric Michaud, Max Tegmark, Mike Williams
core_idea: Grokking = delayed generalization explained by a effective-theory of representation learning dynamics.
why_it_matters: First mechanistic theory; predicts when grokking happens from dataset properties.

title: Omnigrok: Grokking Beyond Algorithmic Data
authors: Ziming Liu, Eric Michaud, Max Tegmark
core_idea: Grokking occurs on image datasets too; driven by weight-norm scale — "LU mechanism": memorize large-norm, generalize small-norm.
why_it_matters: Grokking is general, and controllable via weight decay — a knob for generalization.

title: Progress Measures for Grokking via Mechanistic Interpretability
authors: Neel Nanda, Lawrence Chan, Tom Lieberum, Jess Smith, Jacob Steinhardt
core_idea: Reverse-engineers a grokking network: it transitions from memorization to a generalizing Fourier/multiplication circuit; restricted-set "pre-grokking" progress measures predict the transition.
why_it_matters: The cleanest causal story of emergent generalization inside a network; mechanistic interpretability's flagship result.

title: Grokking as the Transition from Lazy to Rich Training Dynamics
authors: Kaifeng Lyu, Zhiyuan Li, et al. (ICLR 2024)
core_idea: Networks grok when they escape the lazy kernel regime into rich feature learning late in training.
why_it_matters: Unifies grokking with the NTK/lazy-rich framework — one theory for both phenomena.

title: Grokking Explained: A Statistical Phenomenon
core_idea: Grokking reinterpreted as a distribution shift between training and test data rather than an optimization mystery.
why_it_matters: The 2025 theory pivot: grokking may be statistical, not dynamical — with direct implications for what "generalization" means for LLM evals.

title: A Survey on Grokking
core_idea: Systematizes all grokking explanations: norm-based, circuit-formation, statistical, physics-based (glass relaxation).
why_it_matters: Entry point to the whole grokking literature; includes 2025 evidence of grokking during 7B-parameter pretraining (OLMoE).

title: Superposition Yields Robust Neural Scaling
core_idea: Neural scaling laws arise mechanistically from superposition — networks storing more features than neurons in interference-prone ways.
why_it_matters: First mechanistic account of WHY scaling laws exist, linking interpretability (domain 03) with scaling theory.

title: A Limit Theory of Foundation Models
core_idea: A rigorous mathematical limit theory for foundation models, extending scaling-law analysis to data quality and training strategies.
why_it_matters: Theoretical frontier (as of 2026): scaling laws are becoming a full limit theory rather than curve fits.

title: Scaling Data-Constrained Language Models
core_idea: Repeating data helps up to ~4 epochs, then returns diminish sharply; unique tokens dominate value.
why_it_matters: The data side of scaling laws — governs planning when internet text runs out; motivates synthetic data and RL data loops.

title: Universal Artificial Intelligence / AIXI
link: https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.0801 (Legg & Hutter, "Universal Intelligence: A Definition of Machine Intelligence", 2007)
core_idea: Intelligence = expected reward maximization over all computable environments weighted by algorithmic probability (AIXI); uncomputable but defines the optimum.
why_it_matters: The formal reference point every practical intelligence (including LLMs) is measured against; Legg-Hutter gives the field's cleanest intelligence definition.

title: On the Measure of Intelligence
core_idea: Intelligence = skill-acquisition efficiency over novel tasks, not skill itself; introduces the ARC benchmark built on core knowledge priors.
why_it_matters: Corrects the benchmark-culture error (skill ≠ intelligence); ARC-AGI remains the reference test for generalization (domain 05).

title: The Organization of Behavior
core_idea: "Neurons that fire together wire together" — cell assemblies form via correlated activity.
why_it_matters: The first learning rule; Oja's PCA (domain 01) and all Hebbian methods descend from it.

title: The Perceptron: A Probabilistic Model
core_idea: A learnable threshold neuron with a convergence proof for linearly separable data.
why_it_matters: First artificial neural network trained by a rule; launched (and, with Minsky, froze) the field.

title: Perceptrons
core_idea: Proves single-layer perceptrons cannot compute XOR; (over-)read as killing neural networks.
why_it_matters: First AI winter trigger; its real lesson — depth or hidden layers are necessary — took 17 years to answer (backprop).

title: Learning Internal Representations by Error Propagation (PDP, vol. 1)
authors: David Rumelhart, Geoffrey Hinton, Ronald Williams
link: MIT Press (chapter); companion: Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams, Nature 323 (1986)
core_idea: Multilayer networks trained end-to-end by backpropagated error signals.
why_it_matters: Reopened the field; every gradient-trained system since (all of them) uses this.

title: Generalization and Network Design Strategies
core_idea: "Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition" (LeCun, Bottou, Bengio, Haffner, Proc. IEEE) industrialized it as LeNet-5.
why_it_matters: The convolutional prior — the strongest demonstration that architecture = inductive bias (domain 01, F2); banks read checks with this in the 1990s.

title: Untersuchungen zu dynamischen neuronalen Netzen (vanishing gradients)
authors: Sepp Hochreiter (diploma thesis, advisor J. Schmidhuber)
core_idea: Gradients through deep/squashing activations decay or explode exponentially — the "fundamental deep learning problem."
why_it_matters: Named the obstacle that residuates every architecture decision for 25 years (LSTM, ReLU, residuals, normalization).

title: Long Short-Term Memory
core_idea: Gated memory cells let gradients persist across hundreds of timesteps.
why_it_matters: THE sequence model 1997–2017 (translation, speech); gates and state-carrying cells reincarnate as the transformer's residual stream with memory roles.

title: Q-Learning
core_idea: Learn action values by bootstrapping temporal-difference errors — no model of the world needed.
why_it_matters: The bridge to neuroscience: dopamine neurons compute exactly this signal (Schultz 1997, domain 04); foundation of all value-based RL.

title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
authors: Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, Geoffrey Hinton
core_idea: GPU-trained deep CNN cuts ImageNet error nearly in half (16.4% vs 26.2%).
why_it_matters: The big bang of the modern era — proof that scale (data × compute × depth) wins; ignited the decade of deep learning.

title: Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases (word2vec)
core_idea: Skip-gram with negative sampling learns vector embeddings where directions carry meaning (king − man + woman ≈ queen).
why_it_matters: Meaning as geometry — the first widely-used demonstration that prediction-trained vectors encode semantics; the "embedding" concept every LLM uses internally.

title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
core_idea: Variational inference made amenable by reparameterization; encoder/decoder learn probabilistic latent representations.
why_it_matters: Founded deep generative modeling; the ELBO objective returns in diffusion theory and in "analysis-by-synthesis" brain models (domain 04).

title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
authors: Ilya Sutskever, Oriol Vinyals, Quoc Le
core_idea: Encode a sentence into a fixed vector, then decode it into another language.
why_it_matters: Established the encoder-decoder paradigm — and its fixed-vector bottleneck, which attention (next entry) was invented to remove.

title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
authors: Dzmitry Bahdanau, Kyunghyun Cho, Yoshua Bengio
core_idea: Attention: the decoder dynamically looks back at all encoder states instead of one vector.
why_it_matters: Invented attention as a soft, differentiable lookup — the mechanism the transformer made foundational (domain 03).

title: Generative Adversarial Networks
core_idea: Generator and discriminator locked in adversarial minimax; sample generation without explicit likelihoods.
why_it_matters: Adversarial self-play as a learning signal — concept recycled in debate-based alignment and adversarial eval (domain 05); also the instability case study that made the field take training dynamics seriously.

title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
core_idea: Per-parameter adaptive moments; robust default step sizes.
why_it_matters: The optimization workhorse (with AdamW variant) behind essentially all deep learning including LLM pretraining.

title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training
core_idea: Normalize layer inputs per minibatch to stabilize activation statistics.
why_it_matters: Made very deep training stable; its successor LayerNorm/RMSNorm is a fixed component of every transformer block.

title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
authors: Kaiming He, Xiangyu Zhang, Shaoqing Ren, Jian Sun
core_idea: Learn residual functions with identity shortcuts → 100+ layer networks trainable.
why_it_matters: The residual stream is the transformer's backbone; loss-landscape geometry (domain 01, F7) explains WHY it works. Arguably the most reused architectural idea in history.

title: Human-Level Control Through Deep Reinforcement Learning
core_idea: Deep Q-network: CNN + Q-learning + experience replay + target networks learns Atari from raw pixels.
why_it_matters: First human-level learning from raw perception; experience replay explicitly borrowed from hippocampal replay (domain 04) — the neuro-AI transfer landmark.

title: Neural Turing Machines
authors: Alex Graves, Greg Wayne, Ivo Danihelka
core_idea: Differentiable external memory addressed by content and location.
why_it_matters: Opened the external-memory line (DNC 2016) — memory as an architectural component rather than emergent state; feeds directly into RAG and agent memory design (domain 05).

title: Mastering the Game of Go with Deep Neural Networks and Tree Search (AlphaGo)
core_idea: Policy/value networks guided Monte-Carlo tree search; trained on human games then self-play.
why_it_matters: Search + learned evaluation beats pure scale; the template that returns in reasoning models (o1/R1 style test-time search, domain 03).

title: Mastering Chess and Shogi by Self-Play (AlphaZero) / [2020] MuZero
authors: David Silver, Julian Schrittwieser et al.
core_idea: AlphaZero: self-play alone reaches superhuman Go/chess/shogi. MuZero: learns a latent world model and plans in it — no rules given.
why_it_matters: MuZero is the proof-of-concept that LEARNED world models + planning scale — the thesis of modern world-model research (domain 05).

title: Representation Learning with Contrastive Predictive Coding
authors: Aaron van den Oord, Yazhe Li, Oriol Vinyals
core_idea: InfoNCE: learn representations by identifying the true future among negatives — maximizes mutual information.
why_it_matters: The single loss behind SimCLR/MoCo/CLIP and many RL representation methods; predictive coding's engineering counterpart (domain 04).

title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations (SimCLR)
authors: Ting Chen, Simon Kornblith, Mohammad Norouzi, Geoffrey Hinton
core_idea: Augment-crop-contrast with big batches and projection heads alone learns strong visual features.
why_it_matters: Showed the recipe, not the architecture, drives self-supervised vision; killed the label bottleneck for pretraining.

title: Momentum Contrast for Unsupervised Visual Representation Learning (MoCo)
core_idea: Dictionary-as-queue with momentum encoder makes contrastive learning practical without huge batches.
why_it_matters: With SimCLR, established that contrastive pretraining transfers to detection/segmentation beyond supervised ImageNet pretraining — a capability transfer precedent for all foundation models.

title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision (CLIP)
core_idea: Contrastively align images and text captions at web scale → zero-shot classification by prompting.
why_it_matters: Multimodal grounding; zero-shot transfer as a paradigm; the backbone of image generators' text encoders and multimodal LLMs.

title: Deep Unsupervised Learning using Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics
core_idea: Generate by slowly destroying structure with diffusion, then learn to reverse the noising process.
why_it_matters: Planted diffusion; with DDPM (Ho et al. 2020, arXiv 2006.11239) became the dominant generative paradigm — and by 2025 a serious language-modeling paradigm (diffusion LLMs, domain 05).

title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer
core_idea: Route each token to a few expert FFNs — parameters grow without proportional compute.
why_it_matters: Decoupling parameters from FLOPs; the backbone of frontier open models (Mixtral, DeepSeek-V3, domain 03).

title: Attention Is All You Need
authors: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit, Llion Jones, Aidan Gomez, Łukasz Kaiser, Illia Polosukhin
core_idea: Drop recurrence entirely; stacked multi-head self-attention + FFN with positional encodings, trained fully in parallel.
why_it_matters: The substrate of every LLM; parallelism over sequence position is what made internet-scale training tractable.

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
core_idea: Masked-language-model pretraining, bidirectional, then fine-tune per task.
why_it_matters: Pretrain-then-adapt became the NLP paradigm; held every GLUE record on release.

title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training (GPT-1)
core_idea: Unidirectional (causal) LM pretraining + light task heads.
why_it_matters: Chose generation over masking — the path that scaled into GPT-2/3 and everything since.

title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners (GPT-2)
core_idea: 1.5B parameters, web text (WebText) → coherent multi-paragraph text, zero-shot task behavior.
why_it_matters: First public evidence that scale alone induces task abilities without supervision — staged release foreshadowed the capability-safety debate.

title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (GPT-3)
core_idea: 175B parameters; in-context learning — tasks solved via prompts/examples with NO weight updates.
why_it_matters: In-context learning is the property that turned LLMs into a general-purpose interface; launched the entire prompt-based ecosystem.

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
core_idea: See domain 01 — power-law loss across N, D, C.
why_it_matters: GPT-3's training budget was set by this curve; scaling became engineering.

title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (Chinchilla)
core_idea: See domain 01 — ~20 tokens/parameter at fixed compute.
why_it_matters: Explained GPT-3-class models as undertrained; rewrote every lab's training recipe.

title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning? (T5: Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer)
core_idea: Cast every NLP task as text-to-text; systematic ablations of scale/data/Architectures.
why_it_matters: The field's cleanest ablation study; unified interface precursor to instruction models.

title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback (InstructGPT)
core_idea: SFT on demonstrations → RLHF (PPO) with a learned reward model from pairwise human preferences.
why_it_matters: The RLHF pipeline; ChatGPT's recipe. Aligned models differ from base models through this stage, not pretraining.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences
core_idea: Learn reward from human preference comparisons instead of hand-crafted rewards.
why_it_matters: The conceptual seed of RLHF, seven years before ChatGPT; also the seed of reward-hacking concerns.

title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
core_idea: Replace human preference labels with AI feedback guided by an explicit written constitution + chain-of-thought critique.
why_it_matters: RLAIF — supervision that scales with compute rather than human labelers; alignment-as-specified-principles.

title: LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment
core_idea: 1,000 curated SFT examples on a strong base ≈ RLHF-level chat quality.
why_it_matters: Alignment is mostly SURFACE behavior elicitation — the knowledge comes from pretraining; contradicting "alignment teaches capabilities."

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
core_idea: Few-shot exemplars WITH intermediate steps dramatically unlock math/logic at large scale.
why_it_matters: Reasoning as a prompting-recoverable ability; token-space computation begins here → o1/R1.

title: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners (“Let’s think step by step”)
core_idea: A single zero-shot phrase triggers stepwise reasoning — no exemplars.
why_it_matters: Reasoning capacity was already in the weights; prompting merely allocates tokens to it.

title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning
core_idea: Sample many reasoning paths, majority-vote answers.
why_it_matters: Simplest test-time-compute scaling; the "ensemble over thoughts" ancestor of search-based reasoning.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
core_idea: Interleave chain-of-thought with tool/environment actions; reasoning plans actions, observations update reasoning.
why_it_matters: The agent loop — nearly every deployed agent framework (tool use, browsing, code agents) is ReAct-shaped.

title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with LLMs
core_idea: Explore a TREE of thought branches with LLM-guided search (BFS/DFS), value judgments, backtracking.
why_it_matters: Explicit search over reasoning — MuZero's template in token space; big gains on planning-type tasks.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks (RAG)
core_idea: Differentiable retrieval into a non-parametric memory (vector index) fused with generation.
why_it_matters: Separates knowledge from weights — cheaper updates, fewer hallucinations, provenance; the backbone of enterprise LLM deployment.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
core_idea: Freeze weights; learn low-rank update matrices — adapter quality at a fraction of memory.
why_it_matters: Fine-tuning democratized (consumer GPUs); weight-deltas as shareable artifacts; the substrate of open-model customization.

title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention
core_idea: IO-aware exact attention — tiling that never materializes the N×N matrix.
why_it_matters: Attention memory wall broken via systems thinking; enabled long-context training; template for kernel-level AI engineering (FlashAttention-2/3).

title: RoFormer: Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE)
core_idea: Rotate query/key vectors by position-dependent angles — relative positions via complex-rotation structure.
why_it_matters: The default positional scheme of modern LLMs; RoPE-scaling tricks (NTK, YaRN) drive long-context extension.

title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models
authors: William Fedus, Barret Zohar, Noam Shazeer
core_idea: Simplified top-1 MoE routing; trillion parameters with stable training.
why_it_matters: MoE made routine; with Mixtral (2024) and DeepSeek-V3 (2024), sparse routing became the open-frontier default — capability per training-FLOP.

title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
core_idea: 671B-total/37B-active MoE; Multi-head Latent Attention; FP8 training; 14.8T tokens for ~2.8M H800-GPU-hours (~$5.6M).
why_it_matters: Frontier capability at 1/20th the cost of Western equivalents; engineering recipe ( MLA, FP8, complementary-triangle MoE load balancing) now the open standard.

title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
core_idea: Chinchilla-optimal small models (7–65B) trained on curated public data match much larger models.
why_it_matters: Open weights + efficient recipe → the entire open-ecosystem (Alpaca, Vicuna, Mistral lineage); weights-as-artifacts era.

title: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)
core_idea: Optimize preferences directly with a classification-style loss — no reward model, no PPO.
why_it_matters: RLHF-quality alignment with supervised-training simplicity; default in open post-training stacks.

title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning (GRPO)
core_idea: Group Relative Policy Optimization — PPO without a separate critic; advantages from group-relative rewards.
why_it_matters: The RL algorithm that made reasoning-RL cheap enough to run at scale; foundation of R1.

title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
core_idea: Pure RL with verifiable rewards (no SFT data, GRPO) elicits emergent reasoning behaviors — self-verification, reflection, long chains; test-time compute allocated by problem difficulty.
why_it_matters: The defining result of 2025: reasoning is TRAINABLE BY RL ALONE at scale; R1-distill series moved open models to frontier reasoning; second scaling axis (inference compute) mainstreamed.

title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally Can Be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
authors: Charlie Snell, Jaehoon Lee, Sanjeev Raghavan, Avirup Sil (UC Berkeley)
core_idea: On hard math, a small model + optimized test-time search beats a 14× larger model.
why_it_matters: Compute-optimal inference — a NEW scaling law axis; the theoretical spine of 2025's reasoning-model economics.

title: s1: Simple Test-Time Scaling
core_idea: 1K curated examples + "budget forcing" (extend/suppress "Wait" tokens) makes a 32B model rival far larger reasoning models.
why_it_matters: Test-time compute control reduced to token-budget steering — embarrassingly effective; reasoning supervision needs are tiny.

title: The Illusion of Thinking: Understanding the Strengths and Limitations of Reasoning Models
core_idea: On puzzle environments with controlled complexity, reasoning models' accuracy collapses beyond a complexity threshold; effort declines as problems near the frontier.
why_it_matters: The strongest 2025 critique of "thinking" — pattern-matching vs. true search; frames the evaluation frontier (procedural, contamination-free benchmarks like ARC-AGI).

title: In-Context Learning and Induction Heads
core_idea: Identifies induction heads — two-attention-head circuits implementing "copy pattern A→B, complete A→? with B" — as the mechanism behind much in-context learning; forms during a training phase change.
why_it_matters: First circuit-level account of an emergent capability; mechanistic interpretability's flagship (with Nanda's grokking circuit, domain 01).

title: Toy Models of Superposition
core_idea: Networks store MORE features than neurons via nearly-orthogonal directions — polysemantic neurons are a consequence, not a bug.
why_it_matters: Explains why interpretability is hard AND why scaling works (superposition ↔ scaling laws, domain 01 F8/2025 mechanism); foundation of sparse-autoencoder feature research.

title: Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning
core_idea: Sparse autoencoders extract monosemantic features (e.g., "Golden Gate Bridge", "code errors") from polysemantic layers.
why_it_matters: Made features concrete and steerable (feature activation = behavior control); scaling monosemanticity (Templeton et al. 2024) extracted millions of features from Claude — interpretability became an engineering discipline.

title: On the Biology of a Large Language Model (circuit tracing)
core_idea: Attribution graphs trace how individual prompts flow through features and circuits in Claude — planning in poems, multi-step reasoning observed directly.
why_it_matters: (As of 2026) the state of the art in opening the black box; moves interpretability from "what's stored" to "how it computes" — the microscope for F9's emergence questions.

title: Faith and Fate: Limits of Transformers on Compositionality
core_idea: On multi-step compositional tasks transformers form parallel "shortcut" circuits whose error compounds exponentially with depth — they don't do serial abstraction natively.
why_it_matters: Explains why chain-of-thought (externalizing steps into tokens) is necessary, not stylistic; motivates search and tool use.

title: The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration (nucleus sampling)
core_idea: Greedy/beam text is degenerate; sampling from the nucleus (top-p mass) is human-like.
why_it_matters: Sampling strategy is cognition-relevant: model distribution's tail matters; still the default decoding knob in every deployed LLM.

title: GPT-4 Technical Report
core_idea: Multimodal, scaled-up transformer; passes professional exams; (details withheld).
why_it_matters: System-scale evidence of continued scaling returns + multimodality; began the closed-frontier era (benchmarks-first disclosure).

title: Advances and Open Problems for LLMs (survey)
core_idea: Analyzes 27 top models (2023–2025): reasoning saturation, data constraints, efficiency frontiers, evaluation crisis.
why_it_matters: Best single map of the field's state as of early 2025 — use as the "what's actually open" reference.

title: A Quantitative Description of Membrane Current and Its Application to Conduction and Excitation in Nerve
core_idea: Coupled differential equations reproducing the action potential from ion-channel dynamics.
why_it_matters: Proof that computation can be *derived* from biophysics — the template for mechanistic explanation that AI's interpretability now imitates.

title: Receptive Fields, Binocular Interaction and Functional Architecture in the Cat's Visual Cortex
core_idea: Cortical neurons are arranged in hierarchical feature detectors — simple cells feed complex cells with invariance.
why_it_matters: The direct biological inspiration for CNNs (LeCun 1989) — hierarchy + feature + invariance was observed in cortex 27 years before AlexNet.

title: The Hippocampus as a Cognitive Map
link: Oxford University Press (book; place cells: O'Keefe & Dostrovsky 1971)
core_idea: Place cells encode location; hippocampus implements a map-like relational memory, not a warehouse.
why_it_matters: Memory as structured, relational, spatial — the design reference for vector stores, agent spatial reasoning, and episodic memory architectures.

title: Vision: A Computational Investigation into the Human Representation and Processing of Visual Information
core_idea: Any intelligent system must be understood at three levels — computation (what/why), algorithm (how), implementation (substrate) — and levels are separable.
why_it_matters: The discipline that keeps AI honest: transformer = one algorithmic answer; LLM scaling debates are arguments at Marr's computational level.

title: Reactivation of Hippocampal Ensemble Memories During Sleep
core_idea: Sequences of place-cell activity from waking experience are replayed during sleep.
why_it_matters: Offline consolidation as a computation — the biological justification for experience replay in RL (DQN) and for offline training phases generally.

title: Emergence of Simple-Cell Receptive Field Properties by Learning a Sparse Code for Natural Images
core_idea: Optimizing for SPARSE codes of natural images reproduces V1 receptive fields — no teacher, no labels.
why_it_matters: The brain's sensory code is shaped by efficient coding of environmental statistics; the direct ancestor of sparse autoencoder features in LLM interpretability (domain 03, F8).

title: A Neural Substrate of Prediction and Reward (dopamine neurons)
authors: Wolfram Schultz, Peter Dayan, Read Montague
core_idea: Dopamine neurons do not signal reward — they signal REWARD PREDICTION ERROR, exactly the TD error of Q-learning.
why_it_matters: The single most celebrated neuro↔AI bridge: a learning algorithm (TD, domain 02) was discovered in neurons before it was standard in machines (or rather, matched after) — reward prediction errors drive both.

title: Predictive Coding in the Visual Cortex: A Functional Interpretation of Some Extra-Classical Receptive-Field Effects
core_idea: Cortex transmits prediction ERRORS up the hierarchy (feedback carries predictions); explains end-stopping and contextual effects.
why_it_matters: Bandwidth-efficient, learned, hierarchical inference — the brain runs a self-supervised predictive model; the blueprint for predictive-processing architectures and a candidate biologically plausible learning rule.

title: A Neural Global Workspace Theory of Conscious (and Unconscious) Processing
authors: Stanislas Dehaene, Jean-Pierre Changeux (building on Baars' Global Workspace 1988)
link: https://doi.org/10.1016/S1053-8119(03)00067-7 (with Baars 2003 Neuron: "A neuronal global workspace model")
core_idea: Conscious access = broadcasting of a winner-take-all selection through a global workspace — a shared, capacity-limited bottleneck routed to many processors.
why_it_matters: A concrete architecture pattern (bottleneck + broadcast) that inspired MoE-style routing, LLM context as workspace, and modular agent designs (Goyal & Bengio 2020).

title: An Information-Theoretic Measure of Consciousness (Integrated Information Theory)
core_idea: Consciousness corresponds to integrated information (Φ) — the causal irreducibility of a system's parts.
why_it_matters: Influential formal program linking substrate structure to experience; CONTested (adversarial testing 2023 favored recurrent processing over IIT) — include as theory-design lesson: formal elegance ≠ empirical validity.

title: Neuronal Circuits of the Neocortex: The Canonical Microcircuit
core_idea: Cortex is a repeated canonical circuit (6 layers, characteristic recurrence and inhibition) whose connectivity is stereotyped across areas.
why_it_matters: Nature's answer to architecture reuse: one repeated block, specialized by input/output, prefigures layer-stacking universality (transformer blocks).

title: Microstructure of a Spatial Map in the Entorhinal Cortex (grid cells)
authors: Torkel Hafting, Marianne Fyhn, Sturla Molden, May-Britt Moser, Edvard Moser
core_idea: Entorhinal grid cells fire on hexagonal tessellations — a metric spatial code.
why_it_matters: Nobel-recognized discovery of an elegant internal coordinate system; grid-cell-like codes emerge in RL agents (Banino 2018) — convergent evolution of representation between brains and networks.

title: Uncertainty, Neuromodulation, and Attention (ACh & NE)
core_idea: Acetylcholine signals expected uncertainty; norepinephrine signals unexpected uncertainty — neuromodulators encode uncertainty types, gating learning and attention.
why_it_matters: Global state control as architecture: neuromodulation is a broadcast hyperparameter system — the biological template for meta-learners, adaptive optimizers, and context conditioning in ML.

title: Small-World Brain Networks
core_idea: Human brain graphs combine high local clustering with short global path lengths — optimal for segregated AND integrated processing.
why_it_matters: Network-architecture lesson for AI: mixture-of-experts routing, agent topologies, and MoE load-balancing are engineering rediscoveries of small-world design.

title: Neuronal Avalanches in Neocortical Circuits
link: https://doi.org/10.1523/JNEUROSCI.23-35-11167.2003 (J. Neurosci. 2003); see also Kinouchi & Copelli 2006, Nat. Phys.
core_idea: Cortical activity propagates in power-law-distributed avalanches — signatures of operation near a critical point.
why_it_matters: Evidence the brain self-tunes to criticality (maximal dynamic range, information transmission) — matching self-organized criticality in physics (domain 01, F11) and edge-of-chaos results in RNN/attention dynamics.

title: Representational Similarity Analysis (RSA): Connecting Computational Models with Brains
authors: Nikolaus Kriegeskorte, Marieke Mur, Peter Bandettini
link: https://doi.org/10.3389/neuro.06.039.2008 (Frontiers in Systems Neuroscience; concept formalizing Edelman 1998)
core_idea: Compare representations via geometry of pairwise distances — model-agnostic comparison between brains, behavior, and machines.
why_it_matters: The measurement tool of representational convergence: CNN layers ↔ visual cortex correspondences (later Yamins et al. 2014) were established this way; reusable for comparing your model's internal geometry to anything.

title: Sleep and Synaptic Homeostasis
core_idea: Sleep globally downscales synaptic strengths — renormalizing after a day of potentiation, preserving relative weights.
why_it_matters: A biological analogue of normalization and weight decay — "forget the noise, keep the signal"; a design hint for continual-learning systems that consolidate by re-normalizing.

title: Prioritized Memory Access Reveals Planning Networks in the Brain
core_idea: What to replay is itself a computation: expected reward gain × shortcut-to-decision determine replay priority.
why_it_matters: Explains WHY experience replay works and when: prioritized replay is information-theoretically optimal curriculum — directly transferable to RL buffer design and agent memory management.

title: Dendritic Error Backpropagation in Deep Cortical Microcircuits
authors: João Sacramento, Rui Ponte Costa, Yoshua Bengio, Walter Senn
core_idea: Layer-specific dendritic compartments can carry error signals locally, approximating backprop in a biologically plausible cortical circuit.
why_it_matters: Existence proof that error-driven deep learning might be implementable in wetware — and a template for local-learning-rule hardware (neuromorphic, optical).

title: Random Feedback Weights Support Learning in Deep Neural Networks (feedback alignment)
authors: Timothy Lillicrap, Daniel Cownden, Douglas Tweed, Colin Akerman
core_idea: Backward weights need not be symmetric — networks adapt their forward weights to whatever feedback channel exists.
why_it_matters: Kills the "backprop is biologically impossible" objection in its simplest form; enables training on hardware where exact reverse passes are impractical.

title: Towards an Integration of Deep Learning and Neuroscience
authors: Adam Marblestone, Greg Wayne, Konrad Kording
core_idea: Systematic map of what neuroscience could contribute to deep learning: memory, attention, continual learning — with the transfer direction specified.
why_it_matters: The reference agenda for neuro→AI borrowing; use as a checklist against your architecture design.

title: Neuroscience-Inspired Artificial Intelligence
authors: Demis Hassabis, Dharshan Kumaran, Courtney Summerfield, Matthew Botvinick
core_idea: Historical and forward synthesis: reliving the neuro→AI pipeline that produced CNNs/RL/attention, and what remains untapped (meta-learning, memory consolidation).
why_it_matters: The manifesto of the field from DeepMind's cofounder — argues AGI likely requires re-engagement with brain mechanisms.

title: Prefrontal Cortex as a Meta-Reinforcement Learning System
authors: Jane Wang, Zeb Kurth-Nelson, Dharshan Kumaran, ... Matthew Botvinick, Demis Hassabis
core_idea: The brain's prefrontal system implements meta-RL: slow synaptic learning (outside) shapes a fast in-context learner (inside) — and the same dynamics emerge in recurrent ANNs trained on task distributions.
why_it_matters: Unifies biological and artificial in-context learning: prefrontal meta-RL ≈ transformer ICL (domain 03, F7); tells you when learned recurrent state beats weight updates.

title: High-Dimensional Geometry of Population Responses
authors: Stringer, C. et al. (Carsen Stringer, Marius Pachitariu, Nicholas Steinmetz, ... Kenneth Harris)
link: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-1346-5 ("High-dimensional geometry of population responses in visual cortex", Nature)
core_idea: Cortical populations track many stimulus variables (near-power-law eigenspectrum) while remaining decodable — high-dimensional but smooth, no collapse.
why_it_matters: Empirical geometry that neural networks should match; connects to superposition (domain 03, F8) and neural collapse (domain 01) — three views of representation geometry across substrates.

title: Inductive Biases for Higher-Level Cognition
core_idea: Transplant Global-Workspace-style inductive biases (bottleneck, modules, broadcast, attention control) into deep nets for combinatorial generalization.
why_it_matters: The most concrete GWT-to-architecture pipeline — directly relevant to modular/multi-agent LLM system design (domain 05).

title: A Survey on Neuro-Mimetic Deep Learning via Predictive Coding
link: arXiv (2025; PubMed-indexed — search "Salvatori predictive coding survey")
core_idea: Comprehensive survey of predictive coding as a learning algorithm — approximating backprop with local errors, with efficiency gains on edge hardware.
why_it_matters: The 2025 state of a serious backprop alternative: local, online, event-friendly — candidate learning rule for neuromorphic and continually-learning systems (domain 05).

title: Perceptions as Hypotheses: Saccades as Experiments
authors: Karl Friston, Rick Adams, Laurent Perrinet, Michael Breakspear
core_idea: Under active inference, perception and action both minimize the same free-energy functional — the brain literally acts to test its perceptual hypotheses.
why_it_matters: The founding statement that one objective (expected free energy) can drive perception, planning, and curiosity — a template for agents that need no separate reward function. Kept short here; neuroscience context in domain 04.

title: World Models
core_idea: Train a tiny VAE world model and an RNN predictor of its latent dynamics, then evolve a small controller inside hallucinated dreams instead of the real environment.
why_it_matters: First striking demonstration that a *learned internal simulator* can be the training ground for behavior — the conceptual seed of Dreamer and of all latent-imagination agents.

title: Learning Latent Dynamics for Planning from Pixels (PlaNet) / [2020] Dream to Control (Dreamer)
authors: Danijar Hafner, Timothy Lillicrap, et al.
core_idea: PlaNet learns a recurrent state-space model from pixels and plans in it; Dreamer makes it sample-efficient by backpropagating value through imagined trajectories (latent imagination) with a replay of only real interactions.
why_it_matters: Converts RL from trial-and-error in reality to *learning inside a learned model* — the efficiency route to agents that cannot afford millions of real mistakes.

title: Scaling Active Inference
authors: Alex Tschantz, Beren Millidge, Anil K. Seth, Christopher L. Buckley
core_idea: Deep active-inference agents (expected free energy = extrinsic value + epistemic value) match or beat model-free RL on standard domains and solve tasks RL cannot without reward shaping.
why_it_matters: Shows active inference is an engineering-viable alternative to reward-based RL — intrinsic curiosity falls out of the objective rather than being bolted on.

title: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models (DreamerV3)
authors: Danijar Hafner, Jurgis Pasukonis, Jimmy Ba, Timothy Lillicrap
core_idea: A single fixed hyperparameter set masters 150+ tasks across benchmarks, and becomes the first agent to collect a Minecraft diamond from scratch, with no human data.
why_it_matters: First evidence that one world-model-based learner can scale across wildly different domains — a concrete counter-proposal to "one benchmark per specialized RL stack".

title: A Path Towards Autonomous Machine Intelligence (JEPA position paper)
core_idea: An architecture blueprint (Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture) in which agents predict in *abstract representation space*, not pixels, using a hierarchy of world models plus a configurator and intrinsic cost.
why_it_matters: The most detailed published alternative to the generative-next-token path: prediction without generation, planning in latent space, energy-based inference — and it now anchors a real research program (I-JEPA, V-JEPA).

title: Self-Supervised Learning from Images with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (I-JEPA)
authors: Mahmoud Assran, Quentin Duval, Ishan Misra, et al. (Meta)
core_idea: Predict representations of masked image regions from other regions, in embedding space — no pixel reconstruction, no hand-crafted augmentations.
why_it_matters: First large-scale working instance of LeCun's blueprint: representation learning by latent prediction beats generative and contrastive pipelines, validating "predict abstractions, not pixels".

title: Revisiting Feature Prediction for Learning Visual Representations from Video (V-JEPA)
authors: Adrien Bardes, Quentin Garrido, Jean Ponce, et al. (Meta)
core_idea: Extends JEPA to video: predict latent features of temporally masked frames; the model develops intuitive physics (object permanence, action prediction) without labels.
why_it_matters: Moves world models toward the pretraining-scale regime — a video-prediction substrate that downstream agents and robotics stacks can build on.

title: Hybrid Computing Using a Neural Network with Dynamic External Memory (DNC)
authors: Alex Graves, Greg Wayne, Ivo Danihelka, et al. (DeepMind)
core_idea: A neural controller with a differentiable, addressable external memory matrix it learns to read, write, and allocate — inference and manipulation by pure gradient descent.
why_it_matters: Memory as an explicit architectural component (not emergent state) — the ancestor of RAG indexes, agent episodic stores, and test-time-memory architectures.

title: Learning to Reinforcement Learn
authors: Jane X. Wang, Zeb Kurth-Nelson, Dhruva Tirumala, et al. (DeepMind)
core_idea: An RNN meta-trained across many tasks learns implicit RL algorithms in its recurrent dynamics — including exploration strategies adapted to each new task at test time.
why_it_matters: Demonstrates that learning-to-learn can emerge in weights + activation state rather than hand-designed updates; the pre-LLM statement of "pretraining then adapting" for decision-making.

title: HyperNetworks
authors: David Ha, Andrew Dai, Quoc V. Le
core_idea: One network generates the weights of another, so model structure itself becomes a learned, dynamically adaptable function of context.
why_it_matters: Weights stop being fixed parameters and become *state* — the conceptual root of fast weights, hypernetwork adapters, and test-time weight adaptation.

title: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Fast Adaptation of Deep Networks (MAML)
authors: Chelsea Finn, Pieter Abbeel, Sergey Levine
core_idea: Optimize initial parameters explicitly so that a few gradient steps on a new task yield good performance — learn an initialization, not a solution.
why_it_matters: The canonical formalization of "learn to adapt in k steps"; the reference point every sample-efficient-adaptation scheme (including LLM-tuning-as-meta-learning analogies) is measured against.

title: Hopfield Networks is All You Need
authors: Hubert Ramsauer, Bernhard Schäfl, Johannes Lehner, et al. (Hochreiter group)
core_idea: Transformer attention is mathematically equivalent to one update step of a modern (exponential-capacity) Hopfield network retrieving a stored pattern.
why_it_matters: Reframes attention as *associative memory retrieval* — connecting transformers to the Hopfield energy-based lineage (domain 01) and licensing energy-based, memory-centric alternatives to softmax attention.

title: The "Echo State" Approach to Analysing and Training Recurrent Neural Networks
link: GMD Report 148, German National Research Center for Information Technology
core_idea: Keep a large random recurrent reservoir fixed and train only a linear readout — the "echo state" property makes the reservoir a fading memory of its input history.
why_it_matters: Established reservoir computing: dynamics as a fixed feature map, learning confined to a cheap output layer — the low-energy predecessor of today's frozen-backbone + small-adapter designs.

title: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
authors: Ricky T. Q. Chen, Yulia Rubanova, Jesse Bettencourt, David Duvenaud
core_idea: Define network depth as a continuous ODE solved by standard numerical integrators, with gradients via the adjoint method at constant memory cost.
why_it_matters: Makes *continuous time* a first-class modeling axis — the mathematical basis for liquid networks and for architectures that trade discrete layers for physical-time dynamics.

title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
authors: Bo Peng, Eric Alcaide, et al.
core_idea: An RNN that can be trained in parallel like a transformer (linear attention reformulated as a recurrence) and runs in constant memory at inference.
why_it_matters: Proof that recurrence and parallel training are not mutually exclusive — a streaming, deployable alternative to quadratic attention born in the open-source community.

title: Hyena Hierarchy: Towards Larger Convolutional Language Models
authors: Michael Poli, Stefano Massaroli, Eric Nguyen, et al.
core_idea: Replace attention with long implicit convolutions gated by a small MLP, yielding subquadratic scaling to hundreds of thousands of context tokens.
why_it_matters: Showed the attention kernel itself is replaceable at language-model scale — the long-convolution branch of the post-transformer zoo that Mamba later overshadowed.

title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
core_idea: Make state-space parameters input-dependent (selective), so the model chooses what to remember or forget — transformer-class quality at linear time and constant per-token memory.
why_it_matters: The flagship non-transformer backbone: streaming/edge inference, million-token contexts, and DNA/audio modeling — and the template the whole 2024+ SSM ecosystem (Jamba, hybrid stacks) builds on.

title: xLSTM: Extended Long Short-Term Memory
authors: Maximilian Beck, Korbinian Pöppel, Markus Spanring, et al. (Hochreiter group)
core_idea: Modernizes the LSTM with exponential gating and matrix memory (sLSTM, mLSTM), restoring the classic cell's competitiveness with transformers and Mamba.
why_it_matters: The recurrence line did not die in 2017 — a direct counter-demonstration that gated recurrence, properly upgraded, belongs in the architecture search space.

title: KAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
authors: Ziming Liu, Yixuan Wang, Sachin Vaidya, et al.
core_idea: Put learnable activation functions on edges (B-splines) instead of fixed activations on nodes, exploiting the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem.
why_it_matters: Small KANs discover symbolic, interpretable formulas where MLPs fit opaque surfaces — an architecture whose inductive bias points toward compositional and scientific discovery, not just benchmark loss.

title: Learning to (Learn at Test Time): RNNs with Expressive Hidden States (TTT layers)
authors: Yu Sun, Xinhao Li, Karan Dalal, et al. (Stanford)
core_idea: Make the RNN hidden state itself a small neural network whose update rule is a step of self-supervised learning — the sequence layer literally trains its memory during the forward pass.
why_it_matters: Unifies fast weights, meta-learning, and long-context modeling: adaptation stops being a separate fine-tuning phase and becomes part of inference.

title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
core_idea: A neural long-term memory module that *surprises-based* writes and forgets at test time, coordinated with short-term attention in a hybrid architecture that scales beyond 2M context.
why_it_matters: Memory management (what to store, when to forget) becomes an architectural, learned-in-place mechanism — a direct answer to the context-window economics of long-horizon agents.

title: Large Language Diffusion Models (LLaDA)
authors: Shen Nie, Fengqi Zhu, Chao Du, et al. (Ant Group, Renmin University)
core_idea: An 8B-parameter diffusion LM trained from scratch with masked-diffusion pretraining and instruction tuning that rivals LLaMA3-8B on many benchmarks.
why_it_matters: First convincing evidence that the *generative paradigm itself* (any-order parallel denoising vs left-to-right factorization) is swappable at language-model scale, with built-in infilling and controllability.

title: Commercial diffusion language models: Mercury and Gemini Diffusion
core_idea: Mercury (2025-02) ships the first commercial-scale diffusion LLM at 1000+ tokens/sec on H100s; Gemini Diffusion (2025-05) is Google DeepMind's research-preview diffusion model with comparable speed.
why_it_matters: Parallel diffusion decoding turns generation speed from a serial-token constraint into a hardware-parallel one — the first deployed crack in autoregressive orthodoxy.

title: Liquid Time-Constant Networks
authors: Ramin Hasani, Mathias Lechner, et al. (MIT)
core_idea: Neural ODEs whose time constants are states, so each neuron adapts its own clock to the input — closed-form variants (CfC) make them cheap enough for deployment.
why_it_matters: Networks that natively handle irregular sampling and time-warped streams (robotics, wearables, edge sensing) — where fixed-clock discrete stacks waste computation.

title: Networks of Spiking Neurons: The Third Generation of Neural Network Models
core_idea: Neurons that communicate by discrete spikes are computationally more powerful than sigmoid units — even with the same analog noise — when time is used as a resource.
why_it_matters: The theoretical charter for event-driven, sparse, energy-cheap computation; every neuromorphic hardware claim descends from it. (Cross-ref domain 04 for the neuroscience side; not yet covered there as of 2026-10.)

title: Loihi: A Neuromorphic Manycore Processor with On-Chip Learning
core_idea: A 128-core chip with asynchronous spiking neurons and programmable on-chip plasticity rules, consuming milliwatts on workloads that cost GPUs watts.
why_it_matters: Physical proof that learning can run at 3-5 orders of magnitude lower energy than GPU training/inference — the hardware existence theorem for always-on embedded intelligence.

title: SpikeGPT: Generative Pre-trained Language Model with Spiking Neural Networks
authors: Rui-Jie Zhu, Qihang Zhao, Guoqi Li, Jason K. Eshraghian
core_idea: A GPT-style language model (up to 345M params) built on spiking RWKV neurons, generating text with binary event-driven activations at roughly 20x less energy than an equivalent dense model.
why_it_matters: The bridge paper: modern generative LLM architecture rendered in spiking form — connects the LLM world to neuromorphic hardware deployment rather than toy tasks.

title: DeepProbLog: Neural Probabilistic Logic Programming
authors: Robin Manhaeve, Sebastijan Dumančić, Angelika Kimmig, Thomas Demeester, Luc De Raedt
core_idea: Embed neural networks as probabilistic predicates inside a differentiable logic program, so gradients flow through logical inference itself.
why_it_matters: The cleanest mechanism for systematic compositionality: symbols guarantee rule structure while sub-symbolic nets supply perception — exactly the generalization pattern pure LLMs still miss.

title: The Neuro-Symbolic Concept Learner: Interpreting Scenes, Words, and Sentences from Natural Supervision
authors: Jiayuan Mao, Chuang Gan, Pushmeet Kohli, Joshua Tenenbaum, Jiajun Wu
core_idea: A visual parser turns pixels into object programs, a semantic parser turns questions into symbolic programs, and answering is program execution — no program annotations.
why_it_matters: Demonstrates human-like data efficiency and zero-shot recombination on VQA by splitting perception (neural) from reasoning (symbolic) — the architecture pattern behind 2024-25 neuro-symbolic ARC solvers.

title: Abandoning Objectives: Evolution Through the Search for Novelty Alone
core_idea: Searching only for behavioral novelty — with no objective function at all — sometimes finds solutions that objective-driven search never reaches (e.g., the deceptive-maze robot).
why_it_matters: Formalizes that objectives can actively mislead: stepping stones to intelligence may only be discoverable by open-ended, novelty-seeking search — a design principle for generating what we cannot specify.

title: Evolution Strategies as a Scalable Alternative to Reinforcement Learning
authors: Tim Salimans, Jonathan Ho, Xi Chen, et al. (OpenAI)
core_idea: Black-box evolution of policy parameters, parallelized across thousands of gradient-free workers, matches deep RL on MuJoCo while sidestepping backprop-through-time entirely.
why_it_matters: Learning without gradients is embarrassingly parallel and non-differentiable-stack-friendly — the fallback optimizer for world models, agents, and hardware where gradients do not flow.

title: Paired Open-Ended Trailblazer (POET)
authors: Rui Wang, Joel Lehman, et al.
core_idea: Endlessly generate new environments and their solvers together, transferring agents between paired challenges to keep difficulty at each learner's frontier.
why_it_matters: The first working engine of open-ended co-evolution of tasks and solutions — an automatic curriculum generator, and a concrete answer to "where does an endless training signal come from?".

title: Emergence of Linguistic Communication from Referential Games
authors: Angeliki Lazaridou, Alexander Peysakhovich, Marco Baroni (with 2016 antecedents)
core_idea: Two agents invent a discrete language to solve referential games; grounded, compositional-ish protocols emerge from pure cooperation pressure, but drift toward non-human languages without inductive biases.
why_it_matters: The experimental base camp for emergent communication: tells you exactly which pressures (grounding, population, ease) make shared symbolic systems arise — and which make them alien.

title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
authors: Joon Sung Park, Joseph O'Brien, Carrie Cai, et al. (Stanford)
core_idea: 25 LLM agents with memory streams, reflection, and planning in a sandbox town produce believable social behavior (party planning, relationship formation) evaluated by human raters.
why_it_matters: The founding demo of society-scale simulation: LLMs as substrate for social-science experiments, agent economies, and synthetic populations — collective intelligence built from generative individuals.

title: Multi-agent LLM ecosystems: swarms, MCP, agent-to-agent protocols
core_idea: A practical stack crystallizes around standard tool protocols (MCP, 2024), agent swarms/orchestration frameworks, and emerging agent-to-agent communication formats across vendors.
why_it_matters: Multi-agent intelligence is becoming *infrastructure* rather than research demo — standard interfaces let heterogeneous agents compose, which is the precondition for agent economies and collective systems that outgrow any single model.

title: STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning
authors: Eric Zelikman, Yuhuai Wu, Jesse Mu, Noah D. Goodman (Stanford)
core_idea: Generate rationales, keep only those that produce correct final answers, fine-tune on them, and re-generate — reasoning ability bootstraps itself upward from a few seeds.
why_it_matters: The origin loop of LLM self-improvement: the STaR pattern (generate, filter by outcome, train, repeat) is the direct ancestor of rejection-sampling fine-tuning and RLVR-era reasoning training.

title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
authors: Timo Schick, Jane Dwivedi-Yu, Roberto Dessì, et al. (Meta)
core_idea: A model self-annotates where inserting an API call (calculator, search, QA) would reduce its own perplexity, then fine-tunes on those insertions — tool use learned, not prompted.
why_it_matters: The model becomes the dispatcher that decides *when* computation should leave its weights — the learning-side foundation of function calling and of agents that offload exact work to tools.

title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
authors: Noah Shinn, Federico Cassano, Beck Labash, et al.
core_idea: Agents that fail a task store a *verbal* self-diagnosis in episodic memory and retry with that lesson in context — episodic control implemented in language instead of weights.
why_it_matters: Cheap, gradient-free self-improvement: converting execution feedback into natural-language policy updates is now the standard inner loop of serious agent frameworks.

title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
authors: Guanzhi Wang, Yuqi Xie, Yunfan Jiang, et al. (NVIDIA, Caltech)
core_idea: An LLM agent in Minecraft writes its own actions as code, verifies them, and stores verified skills in a growing skill library that compounds across tasks without any gradient updates.
why_it_matters: The skill-library pattern: continual learning as *accumulated executable artifacts* — the most copied mechanism for making agents improve monotonically in open worlds.

title: Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-play Reasoning with Zero Data
authors: Andrew Zhao, Yiran Wu, Yang Yue, et al. (Tsinghua LeapLab)
core_idea: One model both *proposes* tasks (to maximize its own learnability) and solves them, verified by a code executor — AlphaZero-style self-play for reasoning with zero external data.
why_it_matters: A working escape from the human-data bottleneck: the training signal is generated and checked by machine, pointing at open-ended self-improvement loops (and their unsupervised-error risks).

title: OpenAI o3 on ARC-AGI: reasoning models crack (part of) the generality benchmark
core_idea: o3, trained with RL on verifiable tasks plus large test-time search, scored 75.7% (87.5% with 172x compute) on ARC-AGI-Pub — the first big jump on the benchmark that had resisted a decade of approaches.
why_it_matters: Evidence that Chollet's skill-acquisition framing (domain 01) responds to RL + test-time search — while costing enormous compute per task, showing "generality" and "efficiency" are still far from joint. System-scale evidence, flagged as such.

title: ARC-AGI-2: the persistent holdout
core_idea: A redesigned ARC suite targeting the efficiency gap — tasks tuned so humans still solve most while frontier reasoning models score in the single to low double digits at release.
why_it_matters: Even o3-class systems only partially crack ARC-AGI-1 at extreme cost, and ARC-AGI-2 re-opens the gap: a live yardstick separating "skill at scale" from general, *sample-efficient* intelligence (Chollet 2019, domain 01).

title: AI Safety via Debate
authors: Geoffrey Irving, Paul Christiano, Dario Amodei (OpenAI)
core_idea: Two adversarial AI debaters with a human judging only the transcript can, in principle, supervise capabilities beyond the judge's own — amplifying oversight instead of capability alone.
why_it_matters: The core mechanism candidate for supervising smarter-than-human systems: supervision scales with computation spent on debate, not with judge expertise.

title: Measuring Progress on Scalable Oversight for Large Language Models
core_idea: A unified evaluation suite (weak-strong pairings, sandwiching, debate, market-making) for the concrete question: can weak overseers extract truthful behavior from stronger models?
why_it_matters: Turns oversight from philosophy into benchmark engineering — defines the measurable race between model capability and our ability to check it.

title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization: Eliciting Strong Capabilities With Weak Supervision
authors: Collin Burns, Pavel Izmailov, Jan Hendrik Kirchner, et al. (OpenAI)
core_idea: Fine-tuning a strong model on labels from a much weaker one recovers most of the strong model's capability — and sometimes beats the weak supervisor's own ceiling.
why_it_matters: Empirical hope that humans can keep steering superhuman models via weak signals (if generalization conditions hold) — the working hypothesis behind 2025-26 oversight plans for self-improving systems.
